'''Ricardo Mario Ehrlich Szalmian''' (born 4 November 1948) is a [[Uruguay]]an biologist and politician. A member of the [[Broad Front (Uruguay)|Broad Front]], he served as [[Intendant of Montevideo]] from 2005 to 2010 and as [[Ministry of Education and Culture (Uruguay)|Minister of Education and Culture]] from 2010 to 2015.

==Early life and education==
Ricardo Ehrlich was born in [[Montevideo]] to [[History of the Jews in Poland|Polish Jewish]] parents.<ref>{{Cite web |date=2007-09-27 |title=El poder del perfil bajo |url=https://www.elpais.com.uy/que-pasa/el-poder-del-perfil-bajo |access-date=2026-02-13 |website=EL PAIS |language=en}}</ref> He was raised in the [[Cerrito, Montevideo|Cerrito]] neighbourhood and attended public schools, including [[Liceo Dámaso Antonio Larrañaga]].<ref>{{Cite web |date=2005-01-30 |title=Largó Ehrlich |url=https://www.lr21.com.uy/comunidad/166456-largo-ehrlich |access-date=2026-02-13 |website=LARED21 |language=es}}</ref>

From an early age, he became involved in far-left revolutionary groups.<ref>{{Cite web |last=Pereyra |first=Macarena |date=2023-06-30 |title=Acciones concretas |url=https://brecha.com.uy/acciones-concretas/ |access-date=2026-02-13 |website=Semanario Brecha |language=es}}</ref> In 1973, he went into exile in [[Buenos Aires]], where he worked as a chemical technician.<ref>{{Cite web |title=Ehrlich: “Falta diálogo entre gobierno y oposición. Pero acá hay dos partes en juego” |url=https://www.montevideo.com.uy/Noticias/Ehrlich--Falta-dialogo-entre-gobierno-y-oposicion-Pero-aca-hay-dos-partes-en-juego--uc793536 |access-date=2026-02-13 |website=Montevideo Portal |language=es}}</ref> A year later, he moved to [[Strasbourg]], where he completed a Master of Science degree at the [[Louis Pasteur University|Université Louis-Pasteur]]. Five years thereafter, he was awarded a doctorate in Physical Sciences.<ref>{{Cite web |title=Perfiles de los nuevos ministros |url=https://www.montevideo.com.uy/Noticias/Perfiles-de-los-nuevos-ministros-uc98190 |access-date=2026-02-13 |website=Montevideo Portal |language=es}}</ref>

== Political career ==
From 2005 until 2010 he was [[Intendant]] (styled ''Intendente Municipal'' in Uruguayan vernacular Spanish) of [[Montevideo]]. He is from the prominent local [[History of the Jews in Uruguay|Jewish community]].

By profession Ehrlich is a leading [[biochemist]] in Uruguay.

In 2005 Ehrlich stood for the leftist [[Broad Front (Uruguay)|Frente Amplio]] in [[Montevideo]]'s departmental elections and won, gaining 60.9% of the vote. His nearest rival, for the [[Colorado Party (Uruguay)|Colorado Party]], was [[Pedro Bordaberry]], a son of former President [[Juan Maria Bordaberry]], who scored 26.9%.

He was longlisted for the 2008 [[World Mayor]] award.

On March 1, 2010, new president [[José Mujica]] appointed him Minister of Education.
